title: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision Working Paper 45: Lessons on supervisory effectiveness – a literature review
summary: This BIS Working Paper 45 provides a literature review on supervisory effectiveness in banking, defining it as promoting safety and soundness by assessing prudential risks, identifying shortcomings, and using supervisory tools appropriately. The paper constructs a 'house of effectiveness' framework with enablers, three pillars (risk identification, remediation/enforcement, collaboration/transparency), and supervisory culture.
key_points: Supervisory effectiveness is defined as promoting bank and system safety and soundness by promptly assessing risks, identifying material shortcomings, and ensuring timely remediation using the supervisory toolkit.

The 'house of effectiveness' framework includes: (1) enablers/impediments at the foundation, (2) three pillars of risk identification/assessment, remediation/enforcement, and collaboration/transparency, and (3) supervisory culture/risk management spanning across all pillars.
Key enablers include: clear institutional mandate focused on safety and soundness, independence, sufficient powers and resources, transparency rules, and well-designed internal/legal processes.
A credible resolution framework with bail-in instruments and effective deposit insurance supports supervision by reducing moral hazard and providing a credible market exit option.
The paper reviews tools for risk identification and assessment (supervisory reviews, stress testing, data analytics) and remediation/enforcement mechanisms.
Authored by staff from Federal Reserve, ECB, European Banking Authority, Bank of Japan, Deutsche Bundesbank, and Bank of Spain.
Published July 2025 with views expressed being those of the authors, not official Basel Committee or BIS positions.
